C. Demolition or Removal of Man Made Structures
The proposed alignment for the reconstructed roadway will require the demolition or removal of two (2) residential structures, six (6) commercial structures, and the campy over the pumps at a gasoline service station.
D. Resources to be Used in Construction
Labor and Materials, such as sand, steel, stone and clay which are necessary for the construction of this project, cannot be retrieved. In general, the commitment of natural resources involved with the construction of this project would be the utilization of sand, stone, gravel, clay, and topsoil from the immediate environs. Other commitments of natural resources that will be involved in construction will be in the form of steel, concrete, water, petroleum fuels, bituminous materials and lumber. The amount used, however, should be more than offset by the benefits of the more efficient movement of people, goods, and services that would be derived by both current and future generations.
E. Increased Use of Resources Engendered by Use of the Facility
By improving the facility as proposed, allowing smoother traffic flow, the use of this facility is expected to decrease individual vehicle energy consumption. Therefore, the use of the improved facility will not necessarily engender an increased use of energy resources. However, it is to be noted that the trip generations which are attributed to land use patterns and population are in conformance with the data provided by the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission.
